newsitem.title: GERMANY: German TV ratings won't be manipulated - ProSieben.
newsitem.headline: German TV ratings won't be manipulated - ProSieben.

text.p: The chairman of ProSieben Media AG said there was no chance of shareholders manipulating TV ratings of stations owned by ProSieben, which on Monday floated its shares.

Georg Kofler, chairman of the German television company, said on Monday that when the GfK media research group collects viewer data, it excludes households which leave their sets tuned to ProSieben stations for the entire night.

"Because of strict controls, we can eliminate the possibility of data manipulation," Kofler said. "Of course, if people start watching more ProSieben stations (due to its entry on the bourse), that would be a nice fringe benefit."

Industries that advertise distributed nearly seven billion marks ($4 billion) in 1996 for TV ads, he said, largely based on ratings data. ProSieben AG posted nearly 1.7 billion in turnover during the same period, of which about 90 percent came from ads.
ProSieben, the company's largest station, claims a viewer share of just under 10 percent in the German market.
Kofler said the influx of new capital would be used for programming development at the company's two TV stations and possibly for acquisitions. ($ = 1.752 German Marks)
